A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InvisibleInk and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G. Full text comparison and visual inspection support a reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-text generation experiments on MIMIC, Yelp, and TAB, downstream classification results, and appendix ablations and analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including the results in Section 5 and Appendices E and G.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, DClip, Top-k+ vocabulary selection, sampling, and InvisibleInk's privacy-accounting procedure are unchanged. Revisions concern descriptions of baseline guarantees rather than the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MIMIC discharge-text, Yelp review, and TAB legal-text coverage, including the Yelp downstream classification task. No evaluated domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Amin et al., AdaPMixED, and AugPE remain in their corresponding comparisons. Appendix B.3.1 revises the account of Amin et al.'s theory and implementation without establishing a change to the comparator actually evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same models, generation counts, metrics, budgets, and hyperparameter settings. Both versions already use the approximately 25% SVT private-token estimate and specify Tprv = 100 in Appendix D.5; v3's calibration discussion does not change that protocol.

E4.justification: The DClip and Top-k+ analyses, vocabulary-expansion statistics, model-scaling analysis, temperature and clipping ablations, adjacency comparison, and example generations are retained in Section 5.2 and Appendices E–G.

E5.justification: Run counts, confidence-interval reporting, and the estimation procedure in Appendix D.6 are unchanged. Revisions to the interpretation of privacy accounting do not change statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings match across the main text and appendices, including Tables 2–3 and 12–14, the experimental figures, and Appendix G's generated examples. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3.1 replaces the previous sensitivity-error argument about Amin et al. with a variable-batch, rescaled-sum formulation using a fixed, data-independent normalizer G. This revises the mathematical assumptions underlying the baseline critique. Property 9's sensitivity bounds and proof, and InvisibleInk's own guarantees and proofs, remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its accounting advantage: v2 calls grid search the only calibration option and says its privacy cost is neglected, whereas v3 allows estimates of adaptive behavior and says extra privacy cost can arise. The main method contributions and computational-efficiency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes Amin et al.'s adaptive private-token selection from AdaPMixED's data-dependent guarantee rather than grouping them together. Appendix B.3.1 also explains that an inaccurate fixed G affects utility rather than guarantee validity. InvisibleInk's own applicability limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3.1 newly specifies fixed-size sampling without replacement and G = B in the baseline implementation, contrasting these with its theoretical batching and normalization. These are added implementation details, not evidence of changed experiments. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware information, and code/data access instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 replaces the blanket allegation that Amin et al.'s analysis is incorrect with a narrower theory–implementation mismatch, and refines the privacy-accounting comparisons in Sections 1–3. This changes the treatment of existing prior work; the cited-work set remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted paragraphs on baseline privacy guarantees and calibration are rewritten, Appendix B.3.1 gains a theory–implementation-gap heading, and acknowledgments are updated. The overall section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is slightly reduced in size, Table 10 shifts within its page, and Equation (8) moves from page 20 to page 21 as Appendix B.3.1 reflows. Figures and tables retain their content and overall designs.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a more precise and qualified baseline critique by separating theoretical validity from implementation assumptions in Appendix B.3.1. Acknowledging estimation as an alternative to grid search also aligns the introductory claims with the SVT estimate already used in both versions' experiments. These changes improve technical precision and internal consistency, while the unchanged method, proofs, and empirical evidence limit the overall gain.
